newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kubo comments don't mean dlr rise undesirable--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Kubo comments don't mean dlr rise undesirable--MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo's comment on a "strong" dollar, made in the United States overnight, does not mean the Japanese government does not want the dollar to go any higher against the yen, a Ministry of Finance official said on Tuesday.
Kubo had said he supports a "strong" dollar but not necessarily a "stronger" one.
"Minister Kubo's comments were a reiteration of the G7's commitment to a stronger dollar, and do not mean that a further dollar rise would be undesirable," the official told reporters.
"We don't have some certain level for the dollar at which we would think 'a rise above this is undesirable'," the official said.
He also said Japan only wanted the dollar to reflect fundamentals.
Kubo is currently in the United States, where he went to attend meetings of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank governors and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank.

Speaking in New York, Kubo said: "The present situation that we are seeing now is something also to be welcomed by the G7 countries and that was the confirmation we had within (weekend G7 meetings)... We're talking about the strong dollar."
But as for a "stronger" dollar, Kubo added: "Well, this is not actually what was meant by the understanding."
